label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — User-provided input from request.getParameterMap() flows through doSomething() (via Thing2.java which concatenates param into StringBuilder.toString()), then through getBytes() and new String(), and finally reaches the HTML response sink at encodeForHTML(new String(input)). The resolved sink value depends on attacker-controlled input (param) which is not sanitized before reaching the HTML output. Although encodeForHTML is applied, the vulnerable data flow exists and user input reaches the response writer.

evidence.note: User input retrieved from request.getParameterMap() assigned to param variable
param passed to doSomething() which forwards to ThingInterface implementation
Sink: user input flows through encodeForHTML() to HTML response writer
Thing2.doSomething() concatenates param into StringBuilder and returns toString() without sanitization
